content.jointProblem: Can a lightweight product-content or metadata-based recommender, optionally combined with purchase signals, improve product-page recommendations over best-seller sorting with only 500–2,000 transactions per client? The first experiment would test transfer to one client's catalogue using temporally held-out purchases, comparing simple content and hybrid variants against best-seller and category-based baselines, while assessing uncertainty, catalogue coverage and serving cost before considering an online trial.

rationale.text: His research directly addresses recommendation degradation under sparse data and changing catalogues, including practical guidance for resource-constrained SMEs.

sources.quote: PERSEDA addresses the degradation of recommendation quality under extreme data sparsity and rapid catalogue change
a technical guideline document for SMEs seeking to deploy recommender systems on modest computational budgets.

rationale.text: He has tested product-metadata priors for item cold-start, providing a relevant candidate approach when purchase co-occurrence is insufficient.

sources.quote: The KG is constructed from product metadata (category hierarchy, brand relations, material attributes) for a fashion retail domain
These embeddings are injected into a standard matrix factorisation model as a regularisation prior on the item factor matrix.

rationale.text: His work on text features in hybrid recommendation is relevant to testing whether product descriptions add useful information, although the published application used job advertisements.

sources.quote: Item descriptions from a job advertisement portal (340,000 postings) are encoded with mean pooling over final-layer token embeddings
replacing or complementing manually engineered metadata features.

rationale.text: He can contribute evaluation methods that explicitly address popularity bias and the possibility that offline improvements do not translate into online gains.

sources.quote: offline evaluation pitfalls including popularity bias in ranking metrics, and the gap between offline and online A/B test outcomes.
We define and operationalise four group-fairness metrics for items: coverage, aggregate diversity, long-tail coverage, and Gini coefficient of recommendation frequency.

rationale.text: He has prior commercial e-commerce recommendation experience, relevant to translating an experiment into a client-facing prototype.

sources.quote: Ivković worked as a part-time machine learning consultant for a Novi Sad-based e-commerce startup, designing and evaluating their first collaborative filtering pipeline.

constraints.text: The prototype must work with the existing small datasets rather than depend on substantial additional transaction collection; best-seller sorting must remain an explicit benchmark.

sources.quote: with only 500–2,000 transactions per client
We do not have the budget or the traffic to wait for larger datasets.
Simple best-seller sorting actually outperformed the model in our A/B test

constraints.text: Data access must be governed by a data-sharing agreement and use the anonymised transaction and catalogue data offered by the company.

sources.quote: We can give a collaborator full read access to anonymised transaction and product catalogue data.
access to anonymised client datasets under a data-sharing agreement.

constraints.text: Scope integration and company-side work around approximately one developer-day per week, initially targeting a single-client prototype.

sources.quote: We can allocate one mid-level developer for roughly one day per week to an applied research collaboration
A working prototype for one client would be enough to start.

constraints.text: The deployment design must accommodate the company's existing web integrations and client-VPS environment; actual hardware and latency limits still need confirmation.

sources.quote: WooCommerce and custom REST API integrations
Docker for containerised deployments on client VPS environments
PHP (Laravel framework) for backend portal development

constraints.text: Any new user-facing widget strings must follow the company's three-language testing workflow.

sources.quote: we test every user-facing string in all three languages before a build ships
Gettext-based localisation with in-house translator review workflow

risks: Published metadata and text-hybrid results concern fashion cold-start and a large job-advertisement corpus, not an entire store with 500–2,000 transactions. The first experiment must test this scale and domain transfer rather than assume the reported gains apply.

Product-page relevance differs from user-history recommendation. Purchase logs alone may not establish which products were viewed together or whether an item is a substitute or complement; evaluation could therefore favour the wrong widget behaviour.
Catalogue size, metadata completeness, description languages and translation consistency are unknown. Weak or inconsistent content may remove the main advantage over collaborative filtering.
Low traffic and few purchases may make both temporal holdouts and online comparisons inconclusive. No meaningful improvement over best-sellers is assured.
Researcher availability, project funding, timetable and deployment resources are unknown; the company's limited engineering allocation could become an integration bottleneck.
The researcher prefers publishable results or thesis topics. Client confidentiality or restrictions on derived outputs could conflict with that preference unless agreed beforehand.
questions: What researcher time, student support, funding and delivery timetable can both parties commit to for a joint project?
Which client should be the pilot, and what are its catalogue size, active-product count, transaction date range and repeat-customer frequency?
Are stable anonymised customer IDs, order-line timestamps, historical product availability, page views, impressions or session logs available, and what does the data-sharing agreement permit?
Should the widget recommend substitutes, complementary products or likely next purchases, and how will the company define commercially meaningful improvement?
How complete are descriptions, categories and attributes, which languages occur in the pilot catalogue, and are translated versions linked to the same product?
Can the parties agree a temporal evaluation protocol, ranking and coverage metrics, uncertainty reporting and an explicit inconclusive or no-improvement outcome before modelling?
What VPS CPU and memory, response-time target, refresh schedule and integration interface are available, and what budget exists for any external encoding services or compute?
Can anonymised findings, code or a student thesis be published without disclosing client data, and who will own the prototype and maintain it after the pilot?
